verdict.rationale: Snyk documents writing your own code queries with DeepCode AI logic, but only in a single thin marketing line, with no syntax docs and no way shown to share those queries across repositories. The well-documented custom-rules path (write, test, bundle, push to an OCI registry for distribution) is for Snyk IaC config scanning, and those rules are written in Rego, which is not clearly a simple syntax. missing for 10: documented custom SAST rule syntax for Snyk Code, cross-repository sharing of SAST queries, evidence that the rule syntax is simple, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a security-engineer, I can write custom static-analysis rules in a simple syntax and share them across repositories

citations.quote: Write your own queries using DeepCode AI logic (with autocomplete) and leverage the hybrid AI to instantly find matches in your code.
The SDK helps you write, debug, test, bundle, and distribute custom rules written in Rego, which can then be used by the Snyk IaC CLI to find vulnerabilities in IaC configuration files.
once you have generated your custom rules bundle, you can distribute it automatically to one of our supported OCI registries by using the `push` command
